text:
mari: Heads-up — dashboards showing p95/p99 for the same endpoint diverging between the per-route view and the global endpoint rollup. Noticed it on high-priority traffic vs default routing buckets.

jake: saw that earlier, looks like sample weighting mismatch during the route-merge step. p50 lines align, tails differ a lot :thinking:

sasha: can you paste the two views? i only saw the global one which spiked around 10:23 PDT

mari: pasted snippets: \nGlobal rollup p99 = 420ms\nRoute 'hp' p99 = 150ms\nSame 1m window, same endpoint id

eli: wild. are we sampling differently for hp vs default? routing policy splits by header and some requests get tagged with route=hp but sampling config might only tag post-aggregation

jake: confirm — current pipeline: router adds route tag -> request logged -> telemetry sampler applies per-route sampling weight -> t-digest aggregator rollups. But route tag gets dropped for the buffer backpressure path, so a bunch of hp requests land in the global bucket without the tag. Aggregator then does unweighted merge.

priya: so the dashboard shows per-route percentiles using only tagged samples, and global uses merged samples (tagless included). That could explain the tail being heavier globally.

mari: yep. edge case: hp has low qps but higher weight; when tag drops we end up undercounting hp's low-latency samples in the global rollup, leaving high-latency ones dominating.

metrics-bot: deployment note: "telemetry-sampler@staging" rolled at 2026-03-18T09:12Z with sampling-weights v2.

eli: short-term mitigation: show sample_count and sampling_rate on the dashboard alongside p95/p99 so folks can spot this mismatch. Also explicitly label which percentiles are derived from route-tagged samples vs merged view.

sasha: UX idea: add a small warning icon that says "route tag missing in X% of samples" and links to docs on sampling semantics.

jake: long-term fix: preserve route tag through backpressure buffers and ensure aggregator rollup merges use the sample weight metadata. Implementation notes: add "weight" field to t-digest merges and update merge semantics to be weighted-tdigest.

eli: that requires runtime and storage changes. Could be breaking for older rollups. Maybe introduce a compatibility flag and a migration job that re-aggregates recent windows with weights.

mari: alternative less invasive: when route tag missing, infer route by tracing span if present (heuristic) and mark as inferred-tag. Not perfect but helps for hp routes where traces are common.

priya: product ask: we need guarantees for SLO alerts — if global p99 can be inflated by untagged spikes, we might get false SLO breaches. Which view should alerting use?

jake: alerting should use the canonical global rollup for now (what actually affects customers). But we should add a secondary alert that fires when per-route and global tails diverge by > 30% and sample_count_low flags present.

sasha: agree. dashboard change + dual-alert strategy seems safe.

mari: i'll file an infra task for keeping tags through buffers (priority P1 for hp routes) and a follow-up for weighted merges (P2). Also opening a small UX ticket for sample_count visibility.

eli: ping me on the infra task, i can help with buffer trace and propagation. Also want to run a re-run of the quantile checker over last 7 days to estimate how common this is.

metrics-bot: cron job scheduled: quantile-diff-checker will run at 03:00 UTC and post results to #eng-platform.

priya: thanks — once we have that diff data we can decide whether to shift alerting defaults.

mari: thanks all — quick action items: (1) sasha -> add sample_count + warning icon (small PR), (2) eli/jake -> design tag propagation, (3) mari -> create rollout tickets and link to this thread. I'll update when tasks are created.

sasha: starting mockups today, will ping for review :+1:

eli: starting a small reproducible test against staging router now.

jake: adding a unit test for weighted t-digest merge while i prototype the change.

mari: closing loop — if anyone finds other endpoints with similar divergence, drop them here and i'll add to the investigation list.

priya: cc @product-ops — noted.

mari: thanks everyone :rocket:
